title: Choose Baby Log's new look
question: Each card is the real Today screen, by day and at 3 a.m. Keep the roll, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Isotype
options.lineage: Otto Neurath & Gerd Arntz picture statistics, 1925–1940
options.thesis: One drawn symbol means one thing, so “is she eating enough?” is answered by counting, not reading.
options.viewport: Name and age, then one colour field holding what matters now (next feed, or the running sleep timer), the quick-log grid of drawn pictograms, and the last 24 hours as rows of symbols: filled = done, faded = the expected range. After 10 pm everything shifts to amber on warm black.
options.risk: Pictograms must be drawn well and consistently; a weak symbol set would look clip-art.

raised.raise: Colour only carries data: every hue names feeds, wet, dirty or sleep; the chrome stays ink.
1px hairline rules divide the screen instead of frosted cards and shadows.
Tabular figures wherever numbers stand, so times and counts line up in columns.
Done things are marked, not hidden: a given dose or met target is struck or filled in place.

options.label: Discharge sheet
options.lineage: the newborn feeding & diaper log hospitals hand out at discharge
options.thesis: The paper chart every new parent already fills in, made live: a 24-hour grid of ticks with a highlighter on what’s next.
options.viewport: A ruled box with next feed and awake/asleep, today’s sheet as a 24-hour tick grid (feed dots, W and D marks, sleep shading, a red now-line), totals against ranges, then the quick-log cells.
options.risk: Familiar — chart-and-grid is where most tracker redesigns land, and it can feel clinical rather than warm.

options.label: Night sky chart
options.lineage: celestial star atlases, read under a red flashlight
options.thesis: The day is a sky chart: sleep as arcs, feeds as stars sized by amount, the next feed ringed in night-vision red.
options.viewport: A full-width 24-hour dial, a big readout under it (next feed, or asleep for), a three-item legend, then the quick-log buttons.
options.case: Wins on the 3 a.m. scene — parents feel the night-vision red; loses on clarity, since counts vs targets read slower from dots than from rows.
options.risk: The dial is the whole idea; if it reads as decoration, Today loses its at-a-glance numbers.

options.label: Day-out guide map
options.thesis: A cheerful family-outing map: what’s next sits on a big flat island, every log button is a coloured capsule.
options.viewport: Baby chip and bell, a green island holding next feed (or the sleep timer) with its action capsule, the eight log capsules, totals in a row.
options.case: Wins on warmth — it feels like family life, not a clinic; loses on clarity, with no icons and counts as bare numbers.
options.risk: Playful can tip into toy-like for medical moments (fever, doses).

options.label: Lexicon page
options.thesis: Black text on a fixed measure, colour quarantined in bordered plates.
options.viewport: Guide words at the head, entries as dense text, charts as plates.
options.case: Loses both: dense text is wrong for one thumb at 3 a.m., and parents don’t live in reference books.
options.kept: Colour only carries data — the chrome stays ink.
options.risk: Reads as a document, not an app.

options.label: Design annual plates
options.thesis: Near-white stock, registration marks, hairlines, one grotesque.
options.viewport: A gallery sheet of plates with credit rows.
options.case: Loses both: reads as an agency portfolio, not a parent’s tool.
options.kept: Hairline rules instead of cards and shadows.

options.label: Datamatics field
options.thesis: Pure black and white barcode fields and strobing lattices.
options.viewport: A barcode field of the day’s events.
options.case: Loses both: strobing black-and-white is hostile to a tired parent and a sleeping room.
options.kept: Tabular figures that align in columns.

options.label: Convention catalog
options.thesis: Thousands of stamp-sized cells on newsprint, circled in pen.
options.viewport: A dense grid of cells keyed to a map.
options.case: Loses both: too dense and too niche for this audience.
options.kept: Done things are marked in place, not hidden.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What baby trackers ship, done impeccably: white, soft pastel accents, rounded cards, friendly illustrated icons.
canonCard.viewport: Summary cards for the last feed, diaper and sleep, a big add button, a timeline below.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other baby app by design.
